TWO MORE SIGHTINGS, 2026-08-22: `gh pr merge` printed `git: 'remote-https' is not a git command` on PR #296 and again on PR #297. Both merges HAD ALREADY LANDED server-side. The rule worked — `gh pr view --json state,mergedAt` was read after each, neither was wrongly retried, and main was synced by hand.

RUNNING COUNT: 5 (2026-08-14) + 4 (2026-08-19, PRs #248/#250/#251/#253) + 2 (today) = AT LEAST 11. This node exists because nothing else was incrementing it.

⭐ THE NEW FINDING IS SHARPER THAN 'NOBODY WAS COUNTING', AND IT IS ABOUT THE GRAPH RATHER THAN ABOUT gh. `fact:the-gh-merge-failure-is-snap-confinement-and-nobody-was-counting` had ALREADY root-caused this on 2026-08-19 — gh is snap-packaged, snap confinement hands it a sandboxed git with no `remote-https` helper, the system git is fine, and the remedy is one package change. THREE DAYS LATER A SESSION HIT THE SAME ERROR TWICE, DIAGNOSED IT FROM SCRATCH, AND WROTE 'second occurrence, so it is a reliable pattern' INTO ITS HANDOFF NOTE — while a node saying 'nine occurrences, here is the cause, here is the fix' sat in the graph, findable by the error string. Anthony had to say 'I'm seeing it again' before anybody searched.

SO THE 2026-08-19 DIAGNOSIS WAS INCOMPLETE, NOT WRONG. It framed the problem as the graph holding the LESSON but not the ONGOING COST. Today shows the graph also held the ROOT CAUSE and the REMEDY, and that was not enough either. A counting mechanism would not have prevented this: the session never looked. The gap is not accumulation, it is SURFACING — nothing puts a known root cause in front of the session at the moment it hits the symptom. That is the third leg again (`fact:vocabulary-needs-three-legs-and-a-users-project-gets-none-of-it`), landing on the project's own operational knowledge instead of on a user's design vocabulary.

⚠️ AND THE COST IS NOW MEASURABLE IN A SECOND CURRENCY. Beyond the per-merge workaround, this cost one session a full re-derivation — environment probing, package inspection, a wrong confidence claim written into durable memory — to reach a conclusion that was already written down. A recurring failure whose fix is known also spends the time of everyone who meets it fresh.

🛑 THE FIX IS BLOCKED ON PHYSICAL ACCESS, NOT ON A DECISION. Anthony chose it on 2026-08-22 (`sudo snap remove gh && sudo apt install gh` — gh 2.45.0-1ubuntu0.3 is already in noble-updates/universe, so no keyring and no third-party repo are needed) and could not run it: he was driving the session REMOTELY FROM A PHONE and has no sudo there. It waits until he is at the dev box. Recorded so the next session does not re-litigate a settled choice, and does not read the continued failures as the decision being open.
